rows.verified: ORR guidance provides rail companies with an approach to managing staff-fatigue risk and good practice.
The current guidance supersedes ORR's 2012 rail-fatigue guidance.
The guidance uses a Plan, Do, Check, Act management approach.
ORR defines fatigue as reduced mental or physical capability arising from factors including sleep loss, extended wakefulness and circadian disruption.
Fatigue can reduce alertness, information processing, reaction speed and decision-making ability.
Rail employers must assess and control fatigue risk for safety-critical and non-safety-critical staff.
Basic fatigue controls are expected even where there is no shift work or significant overtime.
A proportionate Fatigue Risk Management System is appropriate where staff work shifts, significant overtime or safety-critical duties.
Rail-fatigue risk depends on roster design, shift timing, overtime, travel, workload, sleep opportunity, health and individual factors.
ORR fatigue evidence is organisation-, role-, roster-, worker-, operation- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level accident probability.
Influenza is an acute viral infection of the respiratory tract.
Influenza A and B viruses cause most clinical influenza illness.
Influenza is highly infectious and usually has an incubation period of 1 to 3 days.
The UKHSA influenza Green Book chapter provides immunisation information for public-health professionals.
The influenza Green Book page was updated on 14 May 2026.
The May 2026 update added advice concerning people experiencing homelessness.
The May 2025 revision updated co-administration, seasonal timing, vaccine terminology, surveillance, uptake, risk groups and occupational-health information.
Seasonal programme delivery should follow the current Green Book and programme guidance rather than old printed schedules.
Influenza risk depends on circulating strain, season, age, comorbidity, exposure, vaccine uptake and vaccine match.
UKHSA influenza evidence is person-, season-, strain-, programme-, exposure- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level illness probability.
